takeaway: Still classic rainy season for the next few days: warm, partly cloudy mornings with a chance of an early coastal shower, then afternoon thunderstorms, with a tropical wave passing Friday. The Caribbean trade winds, which blow offshore at Nosara, still arrive Sunday, but the marine forecast now cuts them shorter, turning the wind southeast to south by Monday night. The models still keep the trades going through much of next week, so treat Sunday and Monday mornings as the surest offshore window. A long-period south-southwest swell keeps running, with a fresh pulse due early next week. No storm threatens Costa Rica. Multi-day soaking rain stays watch-only, with a small uptick in the Oct 16–19 signal.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Thu–Sat, Oct 8–10)
periods.pattern: Local heating runs the show. Costa Rica's weather service expects a partly cloudy morning with possible coastal showers on the Pacific side, then a high chance of afternoon storms spreading from the mountains onto the Guanacaste lowlands, and possible rain on the Nicoya Peninsula tonight. Nicoya tops out near 32–33°C today. A tropical wave crosses Friday, which keeps early-morning showers possible along the coast through the weekend. Model averages show light to moderate daily rain on the peninsula and heavier rain in the mountains, easing a bit Saturday.
periods.implications: Mornings are the best window for anything outdoors, though a quick early shower is possible Friday. Expect stormy afternoons with lightning, and some rain in the evening.
periods.confidence: High on the sunny-morning, stormy-afternoon rhythm. Moderate on exactly when cells hit Nosara.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Sun–Wed, Oct 11–14)
periods.pattern: The trades push across Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica from Sunday, and every model shows them at their strongest Sunday night into Tuesday. The heaviest rain shifts offshore to the south and west of us. The marine forecast, though, brings the wind around to southeast and then south by Monday night, as a low starts forming south of Guatemala. The U.S. hurricane center now gives that low a 50% chance of becoming a tropical depression within a week, moving away to the west-northwest.
periods.implications: Fewer and weaker afternoon storms on our side are likely from Sunday, with Sunday and Monday the cleanest days. Tuesday and Wednesday are less certain and could bring back some showers if the wind turns southerly.
periods.confidence: High that the trades arrive Sunday. Moderate on how long they last at the coast past Monday.

periods.label: Days 8–15 (Thu–Thu, Oct 15–22)
periods.pattern: The European ensembles, both the AI and standard versions, keep easterly winds over Nicaragua and Costa Rica through about Oct 20, with the heavier rain on the Caribbean coast and lighter rain on our side. The U.S. ensemble has the trades fading around Oct 14–16, with a low south of Guatemala around Oct 18 and a wetter Pacific coast Oct 16–19. The latest U.S. main model run goes further, with a low drifting close to northern Costa Rica around Oct 16–18, but it's on its own. Costa Rica's long-range outlook still calls for less rain than normal Oct 12–25 and very dry weather from about Oct 26.
periods.implications: Leans drier than a normal October, but the Oct 16–19 stretch is the one to watch before locking in rain-sensitive plans.
periods.confidence: Low to moderate. The European and U.S. models split on that low.

surfWinds.regime: Light and variable through Saturday (north to northwest at times), then Caribbean trades (offshore at Nosara) Sunday into Monday. The marine forecast turns the wind southeast to south Monday night.
surfWinds.detail: The Papagayo marine forecast (issued 2:35 a.m. PDT Thursday) has north wind around 10 knots this morning, going variable under 5 knots, then north to northwest around 10 knots late tonight. Friday is north around 10 knots, and Saturday turns north to northeast around 10 knots. North is close to cross-shore here, and northwest is side-onshore. Light and variable doesn't mean glassy offshore. It just means no trade wind, so the sea breeze still takes over by late morning. Sunday goes northeast to east 10–15 knots and Sunday night east 10–15 knots. That's the real Caribbean trade, offshore for Nosara. Monday turns east to southeast, then southeast to south 10–15 knots Monday night, which is cross-shore to side-onshore. Seas are 4–6 feet in a south-southwest swell with long 17-second periods today, easing to about 14–15 seconds over the weekend. A new pulse of 5–7 feet at about 16 seconds shows up Monday night. Nicaragua: the models show the trades blowing across Nicaragua and out over the Pacific Sunday through Tuesday, and the European models keep them going to about Oct 20. All-day offshore in Nicaragua would point to strong, clean Nosara mornings, but it doesn't mean all-day offshore here, and the marine forecast's southerly turn Monday night is the reason for caution.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Through Saturday, dawn patrol before the sea breeze fills in. The long-period swell is worth getting up for. Sunday morning through Monday morning (Oct 11–12) is the best offshore window, possibly holding later in the day Sunday. Tuesday's new swell could be good early if the trades hang on, but plan on a shorter morning window.
surfWinds.confidence: High on light winds through Saturday and the trades arriving Sunday. Moderate on Monday. Low to moderate on Tuesday onward.

gyreWatch.status: Watch only, nothing established. A small uptick from yesterday.
gyreWatch.possibleTiming: Oct 16–19, mostly from the U.S. models, with the wet area mainly just offshore.
gyreWatch.supporting: The hurricane center raised the chance of a tropical depression south of Guatemala to 50% within a week (up from 30%). The U.S. ensemble puts a low south of Guatemala around Oct 18 and spreads heavier rain over the Pacific waters off Central America Oct 16–19. The latest U.S. main model run brings a low close to northern Costa Rica around Oct 16–18, with southwest winds feeding into the country, which is the kind of setup that brings multi-day rain. The marine forecast's turn to southerly winds Monday night fits a low starting to draw Pacific air in.
gyreWatch.conflicting: Both European ensembles keep easterly trades over Costa Rica through about Oct 20 and put the heavier rain on the Caribbean coast, which normally means a drier Pacific side. The hurricane center expects the low to move away to the west-northwest. The U.S. main model's close-in low has no support from the ensemble averages. Costa Rica's long-range outlook calls for less rain than normal Oct 12–25 with no extreme events, and the U.S. tropics outlook, last updated Oct 6, expects below-normal Caribbean rain and doesn't mention a Central American gyre.

whatChanged: The marine forecast now runs through Monday night and turns the trades southeast to south by then. Yesterday it simply had northeast to east wind Sunday night. Saturday now leans north to northeast instead of northwest. The hurricane center raised the low south of Guatemala to a 50% chance (from 30%). The U.S. models are wetter for Oct 16–19 and the main U.S. run brings a low near northern Costa Rica, while the European models still hold the trades through about Oct 20. A new swell pulse now shows for Monday night. Costa Rica's weather service hasn't issued a new alert since Tuesday, and its weekly and long-range outlooks haven't changed. Today's high at Nicoya is a little cooler, about 32.5°C against 34.5°C yesterday.
practical: Get outside in the morning and plan around afternoon storms through Saturday, with a possible early shower Friday from the tropical wave. Surf dawn patrol for the long-period swell. Circle Sunday and Monday (Oct 11–12) for the cleanest offshore mornings. Keep Oct 16–19 flexible until the models agree on that low. No tropical storm threat to Costa Rica.
